observations_and_questions.classification: source-level documentation/policy mismatch; no product failure or global unique count asserted
observations_and_questions.trace: The resampling helper says it splits each edge into segments no longer than target_edge. The public triangulate entry supplies no counts, so the helper uses round(length/target_edge) with a minimum of one. The selected garment build independently computes the same rounded initial counts and passes them to the helper, raising counts to match linked seams. For a positive target and an edge length exactly 1.25 times target with no seam-driven increase, the ratio rounds to one, and the resulting boundary segment spans the whole 1.25-times-target edge. This is integer and real-number source reasoning only.
observations_and_questions.limits: The public entry and garment build describe target_edge as an aim or resolution knob, not expressly a strict maximum. No supported physical producer with that ratio, generated mesh, seam, solver, visual effect or runtime behavior is established. The private helper documentation and actual stated product policy must be reconciled before treating this as a geometric defect. Original q614 covers broader mesh quality, but an exact alias is unproved.
observations_and_questions.future_direction: Establish whether target is an approximate spacing or a hard maximum, including seam matching and tolerances. If hard, update the shared subdivision admission and count policy coherently; if approximate, correct the narrow helper documentation. Preserve seam correspondence and budget behavior; no implementation or validation performed.

observations_and_questions.classification: source-proven documentation discrepancy; consumer impact unknown
observations_and_questions.trace: The public signed_area documentation says twice the signed polygon area, but the implementation multiplies the shoelace sum by one half, the conventional signed area. Sign and zero are unaffected; a consumer relying on the stated magnitude would have a factor-of-two expectation mismatch.
observations_and_questions.limits: This is source arithmetic and public documentation comparison, not an executed computation. A scoped 95e text search found the same module tests call it; matching names in other modules do not establish a call to this function. External callers and intended contract are unknown.
observations_and_questions.future_direction: Confirm the public return contract and correct documentation or the implementation at the owner as needed, preserving any valid area consumers; no change made.

observations_and_questions.classification: original q614 and rig admission questions independently revisited; no duplicate unique count
observations_and_questions.trace: Triangulate rejects fewer than three points, nonpositive target and NaN, then resamples, adds interior points and filters unconstrained Delaunay triangles by centroid. A centroid inside a concave polygon alone does not prove every point of the triangle is inside; the source contains no explicit constrained-edge check here. Public contains subtracts one from outline length, but the selected triangulate route first guards length at least three.
observations_and_questions.limits: No output triangle, input polygon, arithmetic panic, geometry, fixture or solver was run. This logic does not prove an actual Delaunay triangle crossing a supported outline. Finite/simple-outline contracts, allowable target infinity, numeric scale, resource/vertex-width limits and actual producer/solver boundaries remain open; public direct contains callers are separate.

nonfindings: A one-line topology re-export identifies the real owner; it is not by itself a duplicate implementation or deprecated compatibility fallback.
The selected triangulate path protects internal contains and interior_points from empty outlines; the distinct public direct contains API is not thereby fully admitted.

Each generated boundary chain starts with a previously created endpoint and has at least one segment by construction under representable finite/resource assumptions; no ordinary previous-chain empty unwrap is established.
The algorithm keeps input winding so seam edge numbering remains stable; reverse winding is not treated as automatically erroneous.
Equal-name or same-unit types elsewhere are not presumed identical semantic owners.

What direct callers use public contains on empty input, and what API admission contract do they expect?
What are the current shell/native solver, scale, mass and alias obligations after triangulation?

thirteen_lenses.producer-propagation: Selected garment builder prepares segment counts and routes panel geometry into triangulation, then into shell topology and mass; other producer and solver owners remain open.
thirteen_lenses.existing-type-owners: Cloth topology re-exports fabelgeist_shell topology; do not invent another owner or transfer canonical-body credit from the re-export.
thirteen_lenses.admission-contracts: Selected triangulate guard rejects short outlines, nonpositive and NaN target but not all nonfinite/simple/count states; public contains has its own admission policy.
thirteen_lenses.invariant-operations: Rounding produces target-sized approximate subdivisions, not the strict maximum in the helper comment; count/width arithmetic and supported budgets require policy.
thirteen_lenses.aggregate-states: PanelMesh vertices, triangles and chains must correlate; the generated path builds this relationship but public fields/default alone do not certify arbitrary mutations.
thirteen_lenses.wrong-duplicate-owners: Single shell topology owner supplies stretch/bend derivation; source identity and particular solver semantics stay separately traced.
thirteen_lenses.redundant-authority: Garment and fallback triangulation independently round segment counts; their combined contract and seam raises require a common resolution policy, but duplication alone is not a new finding.
thirteen_lenses.behavior-preservation: Keep input edge order and seam correspondence across any future refinement; preserve documented legal empty/default and nonmanifold behavior once actual policies are decided.
thirteen_lenses.enum-state-shape: Default empty mesh represents an intentional low-level outcome, whereas garment build has error returns for selected invalid target and seams. No universal enum replacement is inferred.
thirteen_lenses.derivability: PanelMesh derives Default and clone/debug; manual geometry math, loop state and numeric tolerance have algorithmic semantics and are not equivalent to trivial derives.
thirteen_lenses.granularity: Panel vertex indices, edge-chain indices, geometry coordinates and target length have distinct semantic units and owners; exact typing must follow the checked geometry boundary.
thirteen_lenses.raw-strings: The inspected triangulator exposes no runtime semantic string API; caller errors are diagnostic text, with reason taxonomy outside this bounded scope.
thirteen_lenses.raw-primitives: Target length, clearances, dimensional area thresholds, Delaunay scales and u32 index limits have different units and purposes; thresholds need actual error budgets rather than blanket constant replacement.
